corrections.why: 'not a change to the six-leg runner' → '... of round 12'. Pure disambiguation, no pointer; consistent with the scope note 'the historical runner' at SKILL.md:1506. Meaning unchanged.

Bound gains 'on this host in this environment'. Grounded at doc:29 ('back to back, on one host, in one environment') and the tool's own limitation text at repeat-control.py:94 ('it is not a determinism proof and it cures no flakiness'). Tightens the bound; Decision 'controls_match' unchanged.

Observation 'Any available controls differ' → 'All runs executed and any differ in exit or either stream'. This deliberately changes the trigger condition to the tool's real precedence: classify() at repeat-control.py:206-210 returns command_unavailable if ANY run did not execute, so controls_mismatch requires all runs executed plus a tuple difference (:211-219). The base wording misdescribed the tool (a mismatch among available runs with one unavailable yields command_unavailable, exit 2, not controls_mismatch). Decision label and Bound unchanged; the correction fixes semantics, it does not drift.

Decision gains '(`baseline_nonzero` / `command_unavailable`, exit 2)'. Both labels and exits are the tool's: repeat-control.py:125-126 maps baseline_nonzero→2 and command_unavailable→2; precedence at :206-219 ('a stable nonzero baseline' = all tuples equal, exit≠0 → baseline_nonzero; 'any run whose command could not be executed' → command_unavailable). 'Equal nonzero controls' keeps its base sense. New pointers are right.
